cards.text: Moses, Israel's leader, has the whole congregation of Israel on the move. They leave the Desert of Sin, moving from place to place as the LORD commanded, and they set up camp at Rephidim. Nice spot, baker, with just ONE little problem.

cards.question: The whole congregation of Israel just camped at Rephidim. What's missing there?

answers.text: Water for the people to drink

cards.text: So the people come straight at Moses: “Give us water to drink.” That's not a question, friend, that's a customer slamming both hands on the counter at closing time.

cards.question: Moses asks the people why they're arguing with him. Then he says they're really doing something else. What?

cards.text: But the people are still thirsty. And the grumbling against Moses cranks up.

cards.question: The thirsty people ask Moses if he brought them out of Egypt to make them and their children and livestock die of thirst.
The whole camp is grumbling at Moses, and they're thirsty. What does Moses do?

cards.text: Moses asks the LORD what he should do with these people, and says a little more and they'll stone him. Baker, that's a prayer AND a 911 call.
The LORD answers. Moses is to walk on ahead of the people and take some of the elders of Israel with him.

cards.question: The LORD tells Moses to bring something along in his hand. What is it?

answers.text: The staff he struck the Nile with
The jar of manna from the camp
A horn filled with anointing oil

cards.text: Then the LORD says, “Behold, I will stand there before you by the rock at Horeb.” Friend, Moses is about to strike that rock, and the last time I hit a rock all I got was a DENT.

cards.question: The LORD tells Moses that when he strikes the rock at Horeb, ___ will come out of it for the people to drink.
Moses strikes the rock at Horeb where nobody else can see him.

cards.text: Then Moses gives that place not one name but TWO: Massah and Meribah.

cards.question: Moses names the place Massah and Meribah because the Israelites ___ and tested the LORD.

cards.text: They tested Him by asking, “Is the LORD among us or not?” Baker, that's like standing in a warm kitchen asking if the oven's on.
After this, the Amalekites come and attack the Israelites at Rephidim. This camp can NOT catch a break.

cards.question: Moses picks one man to lead the fight against the Amalekites. Who?

cards.text: Joshua son of Nun, Moses' assistant (Exod 33:11), is to choose some men and go out to fight. But Moses has his own spot picked out for tomorrow.

cards.question: While Joshua fights the Amalekites, where does Moses say he'll be?

answers.text: On the hilltop with the staff of God
On the front line with a sword
Back in the camp with the elders

cards.text: Joshua does as Moses instructed and fights. Up the hill go Moses, Aaron his brother (Exod 4:14), and a man named Hur.

cards.question: Moses is up on the hilltop during the battle with Amalek. What decides who's winning down below?

answers.text: Whether Moses holds his hands up
How loudly the camp is praying
Where the sun sits in the sky

cards.question: When Moses lowers his hands, Amalek starts winning the battle.

cards.text: But arms get tired, and Moses' hands grow heavy. You ever hold your phone up for a group photo so long your whole arm starts SHAKING?

cards.question: Moses' hands are getting heavy up on the hill. What do Aaron and Hur do?

answers.text: Set a stone under him and hold his hands up
Take the staff and hold it up themselves
Run down the hill to help Joshua fight

cards.question: Aaron and Hur hold up Moses' hands, one on each ___, so his hands stay steady until the ___ goes down.

cards.text: So Joshua overwhelms Amalek and his army with the sword. Joshua gets the win, but I see you, Aaron and Hur, MVPs of arm holding.
Then the LORD tells Moses to write this on a scroll as a reminder.

cards.question: The LORD tells Moses to write it on a scroll as a reminder and recite it to ___.
When the LORD tells Moses to write it on a scroll, what does He say He'll do to Amalek?

answers.text: Drive them far into the east

cards.text: Picture Moses up on that hill until sundown, hands held high over the army like a flag on a pole. Now he builds an altar and gives it a name.

cards.question: After the battle with Amalek, what does Moses name the altar he builds?

cards.text: Moses says “a hand was lifted up toward the throne of the LORD.” And he's not done talking about Amalek.

cards.question: Moses says the LORD will war against Amalek for just one generation.

findings.problem: The question says Moses tells the people they're 'really' doing something else. That claims their contending with Moses is actually testing the LORD. The text only puts two questions side by side: 'Why do you contend with me?' and 'Why do you test the LORD?' It leaves the link between them open. Verse 7 also lists quarreling and testing as two separate things. The card also turns Moses' question into a statement.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open. Who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The Amalekites show up for the first time with no word about who they are.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The setup line compares Moses' raised hands to 'a flag on a pole' right before card 16 asks what Moses names the altar. That all but hands the baker the answer 'The LORD Is My Banner' and rules out the other two choices. It also ties the raised hands to the altar's name, a link the text never states.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The card retells Moses holding his hands up on the hill until sundown (Exodus 17:11-12) but cites only Exodus 17:15. Its first sentence also goes back over earlier moments instead of moving the passage forward.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The first sentence recaps the hilltop scene (hands held up until sundown), which cards 6 to 11 already covered, before it moves on to the altar.
